To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The time-dependent properties of the cockroach tibial sensillum are distributed in a non-linear manner among a variety of intermediate mechanisms, including the coupling tissue and transducer membrane of the receptor cell and the encoder of the axon.

(i) in the large campaniform mechanoreceptors of cockroach legs, the time course of adaptation and the sensitivity of the receptor potential to sinusoidally modulate stimuli are both described by linear transfer functions, (ii) the transfer functions for both properties are similar in shape and magnitude to the transfer function of the transducer, and (iii) the time course and sensitivity of the transducer are described by a single parameter, the time constant, that is the same for both properties.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the campaniform receptors in the cockroach tibial exoskeleton are mechanoreceptors having a proprioceptive and a locomotion coordinating function.
the campaniform receptor is an excellent model system for studying the mechanisms of mechanoreception.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the receptor potentials in the sensilla are generated by a strain-sensitive conductance mechanism.

the receptor potential is a useful measure of the time-dependent behavior of a receptor, and that it can be described by linear transfer functions which characterize the properties of intermediate mechanisms of coupling and transduction.

the time-dependent processes contributing to adaptation and sensitivity are distributed among the intermediate mechanisms in a complex way that cannot be predicted by the behavior of isolated mechanisms.
